findings.evidence: BaseChange.lean:201-204: `∃ (P ...) (ψ : P ⟶ K), ... QuasiIso ψ ∧ ∀ S f, QuasiIso (((ModuleCat.extendScalars f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map ψ)`. The PR proof destructures `⟨P, ψ, hP₀, hP₁, hP, -, hψ⟩` and exports only `Nonempty` isomorphisms. Roadmap STATUS.md:38 lists cohomology and base change and Grauert as remaining Layer C work.
findings.fix: Make the ordered Čech complex (currently `private abbrev orderedCechComplex`) a public named complex, together with its computation of base-change cohomology. State the theorem as the existence of `P` with `ψ : P ⟶ orderedCechComplex U M` such that `ψ` and every `extendScalars f` image of it is a `QuasiIso`, keeping the boundedness and finite projective conditions.
findings.issue: `exists_finite_projective_complex_cohomology_pullback` existentially quantifies away the quasi-iso `ψ : P ⟶ K` that `exists_quasiIso_finite_projective` provides, and states only an unrelated `Nonempty (_ ≃ₗ[R'] _)` for each `R'` and `n`. The isomorphisms are not tied to any morphism, so they cannot be compared across ring maps `R' → R''` or with the base-change map `Hⁿ(X,M) ⊗ R' → Hⁿ(Y,g^*M)`. The PR says later stages build on this result, but cohomology and base change and Grauert need exactly that naturality.

summary: The headline theorem drops the quasi-isomorphism ψ and gives only a separate `Nonempty` isomorphism for each `R'`, so later roadmap items (cohomology and base change, Grauert) cannot get naturality from it. `Submodule.mapMkQKerEquiv` is general linear algebra placed in a homology semicontinuity file.
